questions.question: A train travels for \(5\frac{1}{2}\) hours, the first half of the distance 60 km/h and the other half at 20 m/sec. The total distance (in km) travelled is:
questions.questionHtml: A train travels for \(5\frac{1}{2}\) hours, the first half of the distance 60 km/h and the other half at 20 m/sec. The total distance (in km) travelled is:
questions.solution:
Alternate MethodFormula used: 

Distance = (X × Y)/(X + Y) × [Total time]

Here, X, Y are the speeds.

Calculation:

Speed of the train of the other half = 20 × 18/5 = 72 km/h

Distance = [(60 × 72)/(60 + 72)] × 11/2

⇒ [(60 × 72)/132] × 11/2

⇒ 60 × 72/24 = 180 km

This is the distance of one side.

Total distance = 2 × 180 = 360 km

Traditional method:

Given:

A train travels for \(5\frac{1}{2}\) hours

Speed of the train in two half are 60 km/h and 20 m/sec

Concept used:

Distance/Speed = Time

Km/h × 5/18 = M/sec

Calculation:

Speed of the train of the other half = 20 × 18/5 = 72 km/h

Let total distance be 2x

According to the question,

x/60 + x/72 = 5.5 hours

⇒ (6x + 5x)/360 = 5.5

⇒ 11x = 360 × 5.5

⇒ x = 180

So, 2x = 360

∴ The total distance (in km) travelled is 360

questions.question: A car travels a distance of x km at a speed of \(5\frac{5}{9}\) m/sec and returns at 5 m/sec to the starting point. If the total time taken by the car is \(7\frac{3}{5}\) hours, then the value of (x + 3) is:
questions.questionHtml: A car travels a distance of x km at a speed of \(5\frac{5}{9}\) m/sec and returns at 5 m/sec to the starting point. If the total time taken by the car is \(7\frac{3}{5}\) hours, then the value of (x + 3) is:
questions.solution:
Given:-
The distance traveled by a car is= x km
The speed of a car is= 50/9 m/sec

Calculation:- 

According to the question, the speed is \(\frac{50}{9}\)m/sec hence, we need to convert this into km because the distance is in the kilometers.

⇒ \(\frac{50}{9}\times \frac{18}{5}= 20km/hr\)

Similarly, \(5\times \frac{18}{5}=18km/hr\)

⇒ \(\frac{x}{20} + \frac{x}{18}\) as x is a distance. Also, this is a sum of two going and return speeds.

⇒ \(\frac{x}{20} + \frac{x}{18}=\frac{38}{5}\)

⇒ \(\frac{19\times x}{180}= \frac{38}{5}\)

⇒ \(x= 72 km\)

According to the question we need to find out the value of (x + 3)= 75 km.

questions.question: In a flight of 600 km, an aircraft was slowed down due to bad weather. Its average speed for the trip was reduced by 200 km/hr and the time of flight increased by 30 minutes. The duration of the flight is
questions.questionHtml: In a flight of 600 km, an aircraft was slowed down due to bad weather. Its average speed for the trip was reduced by 200 km/hr and the time of flight increased by 30 minutes. The duration of the flight is
questions.solution:
Given:

Total Distance = 600 km

average speed was reduced = 200 km/hr

the time of flight increased = 30 minutes

Formula Used:

\(Average\ Speed = \frac{Total\ Distance }{Time}\)

Calculation:

Let the original duration of flight be t hours.

So, Original average speed = \(\frac{600}{t}\)

Due to bad weather speed of trip is reduced by 200 km/hr and time of flight is increased by 30 mins 

Reduced average speed = \(\frac{600}{t}\) - 200

New duration time = (t + 0.5) hrs

The average speed = \(\frac{600}{(t + 0.5)}\)

⇒ \(\frac{600}{t}\) - 200 = \(\frac{600}{(t + 0.5)}\)

⇒ \(\frac{3}{t} - 1 = \frac{3}{t+0.5}\)

⇒ \(\frac{3-t}{t} = \frac{3}{t+0.5}\)

⇒ t2 + 0.5t - 1.5 = 0

⇒ 2t2 + t - 3 = 0

⇒ 2t2 - 2t +3t -3 = 0

⇒ (t - 1)(2t + 3) = 0

⇒ (t - 1) = 0

⇒ t  = 1 hr

∴ The duration of the flight is 1 hour.

questions.question: One-fourth of a certain journey is covered at the rate of 15 km/h, one-sixth of it is covered at the rate of 40 km/h and the rest of it is covered at 30 km/h. Find the average speed for the whole journey.
questions.questionHtml: One-fourth of a certain journey is covered at the rate of 15 km/h, one-sixth of it is covered at the rate of 40 km/h and the rest of it is covered at 30 km/h. Find the average speed for the whole journey.
questions.solution:
Given: 

Speed to cover one-fourth journey (S1) = 15 km/hr

Speed to cover one-sixth journey (S2) = 40 km/hr

Speed to cover Remaining journey (S3) = 30 km/hr

Formula Used:

Time = Distance/Speed

Average Speed = Total Distance / Total Time

Calculation:

Let, Total Distance = D, and

Time taken are T1, T2, and T3 respectively.

T1 = (D/4)/S1 = D/60 hr.

T2 = (D/6)S2 = D/240 hr.

Remaining Distance =  D - (D/4) - (D/6)  = (7D/12)

So, T3 = (7D/12)/S3  = (7D/360)

Total Time = D/60) + (D/240) + (7D/360) = (29 × D)/720

Average Speed = (Total Distance / Total time)

Average Speed = \(\frac{D}{\frac{29D}{720}}\) = \(\frac{720}{29}\) 

Average Speed = \(24 \frac{24}{29}\)

∴ Average speed of the whole journey is \(24 \frac{24}{29}\) km/hr.

questions.question: One third part of a certain journey is covered at the speed of 22 km/hr, one fourth part at the speed of 33 km/hr and the rest part at the speed of 55 km/hr. What will be the average speed for the whole journey?
questions.questionHtml: One third part of a certain journey is covered at the speed of 22 km/hr, one fourth part at the speed of 33 km/hr and the rest part at the speed of 55 km/hr. What will be the average speed for the whole journey?
questions.solution:
Given:

Speed for one third of the journey = 22 km/hr.

Speed for one fourth of the journey = 33 km/hr.

Speed for the rest of the journey = 55 km/hr.

Formula Used:

Average speed = Total distance traveled / Total time taken

Calculation:

Let the total distance of the journey be d km.

Distance covered in first part = d/3

Distance covered in second part = d/4

Distance covered in the rest part = d - (d/3 + d/4)

Distance covered in the rest part = d - (4d + 3d) / 12

Distance covered in the rest part = d - 7d / 12

Distance covered in the rest part = 5d / 12

Time taken for the first part = (d/3) / 22

Time taken for the first part = d / 66

Time taken for the second part = (d/4) / 33

Time taken for the second part = d / 132

Time taken for the rest part = (5d / 12) / 55

Time taken for the rest part = 5d / 660 = d/132

Total time taken = d / 66 + d / 132 + d / 132

Total time taken = d(1/66 + 1/132 + 1/132)

Total time taken = d(2/132 + 1/66)

Total time taken = d(1/66 + 1/66)

Total time taken = d(2/66)

Total time taken = d / 33

Average speed = Total distance / Total time

Average speed = d / (d / 33)

Average speed = 33 km/hr

The average speed for the whole journey is 33 km/hr.

questions.question: A person has to reach a certain place at a certain time and he finds that he will be 15 minutes late if he walks at 4 km/hr and 10 minute earlier, if he walks at 6 km/hr. Find the distance he has to cover.
questions.questionHtml: A person has to reach a certain place at a certain time and he finds that he will be 15 minutes late if he walks at 4 km/hr and 10 minute earlier, if he walks at 6 km/hr. Find the distance he has to cover.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Distance = (Product of Speeds ÷ Difference of Speeds) × Total Time Difference

Total Time Difference = 15 min (late) + 10 min (early) = 25 min = 25/60 hr

Distance = (4 × 6 ÷ (6 − 4)) × (25 ÷ 60)

Distance = (24 ÷ 2) × (5 ÷ 12) = 12 × (5 ÷ 12) = 5 km

∴ The correct option is (C).

Alternate Method

Given:

Speed1 (S1) = 4 km/hr, Time Delay = 15 min

Speed2 (S2) = 6 km/hr, Time Advance = 10 min

Formula Used:

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Calculations:

⇒ Let the distance be D km.

⇒ Time taken at 4 km/hr = D/4 hours

⇒ Time taken at 6 km/hr = D/6 hours

⇒ Difference in time = 15 − (−10) = 25 minutes

⇒ 25 minutes = 25/60 hours = 5/12 hours

⇒ D/4 − D/6 = 5/12

⇒ (3D − 2D) / 12 = 5/12

⇒ D / 12 = 5 / 12

⇒ D = 5 km

∴ The correct option is (C).

Additional Information

Average Speed for Equal Distances

If a journey is divided into two equal distances covered at speeds x and y, then Average Speed = 2xy ÷ (x + y).

Relative Speed

When two objects move in the same direction, relative speed = S1 − S2. In opposite directions, relative speed = S1 + S2.

Unit Conversion

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.

questions.question: Krishna travels from point A to point B in 6 hours and returns back to point A from point B in 5 hours. Point A and point B are 220 miles apart along a straight highway. What is the average speed of Krishna for the whole journey?

questions.question: The total time is taken by Rohan travelling from point A to B by using the bike and return back by using the car in 2 \(\frac{1}{9}\) hours. If time is taken by Rohan to travel from point A to point B and return back by using the only bike is 1 \(\frac{1}{9}\) hours, then find the time taken by Rohan to travel the whole journey by using car.
questions.questionHtml: The total time is taken by Rohan travelling from point A to B by using the bike and return back by using the car in 2\(\frac{1}{9}\) hours. If time is taken by Rohan to travel from point A to point B and return back by using the only bike is 1\(\frac{1}{9}\) hours, then find the time taken by Rohan to travel the whole journey by using car.
questions.solution:
Shortcut TrickThe total time is taken by Rohan to travel from point A to B by using the bike and return back by using the car in x hours. If time is taken by Rohan to travel from point A to point B and return back by using the only bike is y hours.

The time taken by Rohan to travel the whole journey by using car = 2x - y

According to the question,

x = \(\frac{19}{9}\) hours

y = \(\frac{10}{9}\) hours

Now,

The time is taken by Rohan to travel the whole journey by using car = 2(\(\frac{19}{9}\)) - \(\frac{10}{9}\) = \(\frac{28}{9}\) hours

∴ The required answer is \(\frac{28}{9}\) hours.

Alternate MethodGiven:

The total time is taken by Rohan travelling from point A to B by using the bike and return back by using the car = 2\(\frac{1}{9}\) = \(\frac{19}{9}\) hours

If time is taken by Rohan to travel from point A to point B and return back by using the only bike = 1\(\frac{1}{9}\) = \(\frac{10}{9}\) hours

Calculation:

Let tB is the time taken by Rohan to travel from point A to point B or the time taken by Rohan to travel from point B to point A by using bike.

Let tC is the time taken by Rohan to travel from point A to point B or the time taken by Rohan to travel from point B to point A by using car.

According to the question,

⇒ tb + tc = \(\frac{19}{9}\) hours     ----(1)

Now,

⇒ tb + tb = \(\frac{10}{9}\) hours

⇒ 2tb = \(\frac{10}{9}\) hours

⇒ tb = \(\frac{5}{9}\) hours     ----(2)

Now by using the equation (1) and (2), we get,

⇒ \(\frac{5}{9}\) + tc = \(\frac{19}{9}\)

⇒ tc = \(\frac{14}{9}\)

The time is taken by Rohan to travel from point A to point B by car = \(\frac{14}{9}\) hours

The time is taken by Rohan to travel the complete journey by car = \(\frac{28}{9}\) hours

∴ The required answer is \(\frac{28}{9}\) hours.

questions.question: One third part of a certain journey is covered at the speed of 18 km/hr, one fourth part at the speed of 27 km/hr and the rest part at the speed of 45 km/hr. What will be the average speed for the whole journey?
questions.questionHtml: One third part of a certain journey is covered at the speed of 18 km/hr, one fourth part at the speed of 27 km/hr and the rest part at the speed of 45 km/hr. What will be the average speed for the whole journey?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Assume Total Distance as a multiple of denominators (3, 4) and speed factors, let it be 108 km.

Time for first 1/3 part (36 km) at 18 km/hr = 36 ÷ 18 = 2 hours.

Time for second 1/4 part (27 km) at 27 km/hr = 27 ÷ 27 = 1 hour.

Time for rest part (108 − 36 − 27 = 45 km) at 45 km/hr = 45 ÷ 45 = 1 hour.

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time = 108 ÷ (2 + 1 + 1) = 108 ÷ 4 = 27 km/hr.

∴ The correct answer is 27 km/hr.

Alternate Method

Given:

Speed1 (v1) = 18 km/hr for 1/3 part

Speed2 (v2) = 27 km/hr for 1/4 part

Speed3 (v3) = 45 km/hr for the rest part

Formula Used:

Average Speed = Total Distance / Total Time

Calculations:

⇒ Let the Total Distance be D km.

⇒ Rest part = 1 − (1/3 + 1/4) = 1 − (4+3)/12 = 1 − 7/12 = 5/12 part.

⇒ Time taken for 1/3 part (t1) = (D/3) ÷ 18 = D/54 hours.

⇒ Time taken for 1/4 part (t2) = (D/4) ÷ 27 = D/108 hours.

⇒ Time taken for rest part (t3) = (5D/12) ÷ 45 = 5D/(12 × 45) = D/(12 × 9) = D/108 hours.

⇒ Total Time (T) = D/54 + D/108 + D/108

⇒ T = (2D + D + D) / 108 = 4D / 108 = D / 27 hours.

⇒ Average Speed = D ÷ (D/27) = 27 km/hr.

∴ The correct answer is 27 km/hr.

Additional Information

Average Speed for Equal Distances

If two equal distances are covered at speeds u and v, then Average Speed = 2uv / (u + v).

Average Speed for Equal Time Intervals

If a person travels at speed u for time t and then at speed v for the same time t, then Average Speed = (u + v) / 2.

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.

questions.question: The average speed of a train is 180% of the average speed of a car. The car covers a distance of 990 km in 15 hours. The time taken (in hours) by the train to cover the distance of 891 km is:
questions.questionHtml: The average speed of a train is 180% of the average speed of a car. The car covers a distance of 990 km in 15 hours. The time taken (in hours) by the train to cover the distance of 891 km is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Speed of the car = 990 ÷ 15 = 66 km/h.

Speed of the train = 180% of 66 = 1.8 × 66 = 118.8 km/h.

Time taken by train = Distance ÷ Speed = 891 ÷ 118.8 = 7.5 hours.

7.5 hours is equal to 7½ hours.

∴ The correct answer is 7½ hours.

Alternate Method

Given:

Distance covered by car = 990 km

Time taken by car = 15 hours

Average speed of train = 180% of average speed of car

Distance to be covered by train = 891 km

Formula Used:

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

Calculations:

⇒ Speed of the car = 990 ÷ 15

⇒ Speed of the car = 66 km/h

⇒ Speed of the train = 180% of 66

⇒ Speed of the train = (180 ÷ 100) × 66 = 1.8 × 66 = 118.8 km/h

⇒ Time taken by the train = 891 ÷ 118.8

⇒ Time taken by the train = 8910 ÷ 1188

⇒ Time taken by the train = 7.5 hours

⇒ 7.5 hours = 7½ hours

∴ The correct answer is 7½ hours.

Additional Information

Average Speed

Average speed is the total distance traveled divided by the total time taken. Formula: Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time.

Relative Speed

When two objects move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds (S1 − S2). In opposite directions, it is the sum (S1 + S2).

Conversion of Units

To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply by 5 ÷ 18. To convert from m/s to km/h, multiply by 18 ÷ 5.
